wu: Human Bingo: Students mingle with bingo cards listing traits like 'likes tea' or 'has a car', asking 'Do you like tea?' and marking names. First to get BINGO wins.
wuAlt: Name Chain: Students stand in a circle, each saying 'I'm [Name] and I like [hobby]', repeating all previous names and hobbies.
Two Truths and a Lie: Students write three statements about themselves, two true and one false; others guess the lie.
pres: Teacher introduces a self-introduction model: 'I'm [Name]. I'm [Age]. I'm from [City]. I want to learn English for [Job/Travel].' Uses flashcards with flags and job icons. Checks understanding with 'What's my name? Where am I from?'
presAlt: Guest Speaker: A volunteer student (prepped) introduces themselves first, then the teacher breaks down their sentences.
Video Model: Show a short clip of two people introducing themselves, then pause to elicit key phrases.
prac: Speed Introductions: Students form two lines, facing each other. They introduce themselves with the model, then one line moves. Teacher monitors and corrects 'be' errors. After 5 rounds, students report their partner's name and goal.
pracAlt: Introduction Circle: Students sit in a circle, passing a ball. The holder introduces themselves and asks 'What's your name?' to the next person.
Fill-in-the-Blank: Students complete a worksheet with 'I ___ [Name]. I ___ from [City]. I ___ to learn English for ___.'
ls: Listen and Match: Teacher reads 5 short introductions (e.g., 'I'm Ali. I'm 25. I'm from Casablanca. I want to learn English for work.'). Students match each to a photo on their worksheet.
re: Stand Up If...: Teacher calls out 'Stand up if you want to learn English for travel!', 'Stand up if you're from Oujda!', etc. Students stand and say 'I want to learn English for [reason]!'
prod: Pair Goal Discussion: Students interview their partner using 'Why do you want to learn English?' and note their answers. Then, each student introduces their partner to the class: 'This is [Name]. He/She wants to learn English for [reason].'
rw: Classroom Language Matching: Students read 10 phrases ('Can I borrow a pen?', 'Open your book, please.') and match them to classroom situations (e.g., 'Someone needs a pen'). Then, they complete a personal-details form with name, age, phone, email.
st: Goodbye Song: Teacher leads 'See You Later, Alligator' with gestures. Recap: 'Today we learned to introduce ourselves and say our goals. Thank you, class! Goodbye!'
g: Students ask 'Do you like...?' to fill their bingo cards.
Students repeat names and hobbies in a circle.
Students guess false statements about peers.
Students stand and state goals for prompts.
Partners ask 'Why learn English?' and report back.
Students pass a ball and introduce themselves.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 5-sentence introduction including a hobby.
Support learners: Use a sentence frame: 'My name is ___. I am ___. I want to learn English for ___.'
hw: Record a 30-second video introducing yourself to a friend.
Find 3 classroom language phrases online and practice them.
tip: Use local examples (e.g., 'I want to learn English for a job at the American Space') to make goals relevant. Avoid correcting every error—focus on communication.
